comparison: Both evaluate claims C24-C32 regarding SE identification and characterization. OpenEval finds the evidence comprehensive and well-documented. Peer reviewers raise significant concerns about methodology, particularly the transition from ~2000 SE peaks to hundreds of target genes, poor figure descriptions, and questioning whether this represents a super enhancer versus typical enhancer. Major disagreement on data quality and interpretation.

Both evaluate claims C33-C38 on pathway analysis, survival analysis, and immune infiltration. OpenEval finds convergent computational and experimental evidence supportive. Peer reviewers state figures are impossible to interpret from accompanying text and Figure 1G is not described, making validity assessment difficult. Disagreement stems from presentation quality concerns.

Both evaluate claims C39-C49 on ZFP36L1 characterization (OpenEval also includes C52 on SE-driven regulation). OpenEval finds robust support from multiple validation approaches. Peer reviewers identify critical gaps: marginal H3K27ac differences between subtypes, lack of direct causal proof (requesting CRISPR-Cas9 SE deletion), and atypical peak shapes. Peer review R3 also addresses C52, questioning the causal SE-ZFP36L1 link that OpenEval R4 supports.

Both evaluate claims C50-C51 on JQ1 inhibitor experiments. OpenEval finds strong mechanistic evidence for SE-driven regulation. Peer reviewers explicitly reject this interpretation, stating JQ1 only proves BRD4 regulation and could indicate typical enhancer rather than super enhancer. Direct disagreement on interpretation of pharmacological data.

Both evaluate claims C53-C60 on ZFP36L1-PD-L1 regulatory relationship. OpenEval finds strong bidirectional evidence from multiple orthogonal methods. Peer reviewers provide detailed criticism: effects are marginal, context-dependent (requiring IFNγ), knockdown failures in some cell lines, and several cell lines express ZFP36L1 without PD-L1, suggesting ZFP36L1 is not a key PD-L1 stimulant. Major disagreement on effect size and biological significance.

OpenEval R6 evaluates C61-C70 on SPI1-ZFP36L1 interactions with rescue experiments. Peer R6 evaluates overlapping claims C61-C79 plus C108, covering SPI1 binding, protein interactions, and SE mapping. OpenEval finds strong mechanistic evidence. Peer reviewers identify major gaps: missing SPI1 depletion experiments, unclear why only SPI1 (not ELF1/E2F1) upregulates expression, marginal effects in some cell lines, lack of PD-L1 upregulation without IFNγ, and unclear motif identification methodology. Disagreement on experimental completeness.

OpenEval R7 evaluates C71-C74 on ZFP36L1-SPI1 protein-protein interaction. Peer R6 includes these claims within broader evaluation (C61-C79, C108). OpenEval finds robust evidence from prediction to in vitro validation. Peer reviewers note missing depletion experiments and marginal effects, though specific concerns about C71-C74 are embedded in broader critique of SPI1 pathway.

OpenEval R8 evaluates C75-C79 on SPI1-SE binding site mapping. Peer R6 includes these claims in evaluation of C61-C79 plus C108. OpenEval finds convergent evidence from multiple approaches. Peer reviewers question motif identification methodology and note incomplete experimental validation, though C75-C79 are not the primary focus of peer concerns.

OpenEval R9 evaluates C80-C86 on HDAC3-mediated regulation and feedback loops. Peer R7 evaluates broader set C80-C98 plus C109-C110, covering HDAC3 and ZFP36L1-HDAC3 mRNA regulation. OpenEval finds comprehensive mechanistic insight. Peer reviewers note missing HDAC3 depletion experiments (over-expression could be artefactual), undiscussed figures (5G, H), and need for ChIP validation of direct involvement. Partial agreement with concerns about experimental completeness.

OpenEval R10 evaluates C87-C90 on rescue experiments for regulatory relationships. Peer R7 includes these claims within broader evaluation (C80-C98, C109-C110). OpenEval finds strong evidence from bidirectional rescue. Peer reviewers' concerns about missing HDAC3 depletion experiments apply to this claim set, indicating incomplete validation despite rescue data.

OpenEval R11 evaluates C91-C98 on ZFP36L1-HDAC3 mRNA destabilization mechanism. Peer R7 includes these claims in evaluation of C80-C98 plus C109-C110. OpenEval finds comprehensive mechanistic evidence from stability assays to domain mapping. Peer reviewers' general concerns about HDAC3 experiments and undiscussed figures apply, though the mRNA stability data appear less directly criticized than other aspects.

OpenEval R12 evaluates C99-C100 on clinical correlations in patient tissues. Peer R8 evaluates C99-C106 including in vivo tumor experiments. OpenEval acknowledges correlation cannot establish causality but finds clinical validation important. Peer reviewers question patient selection (why three patients shown), lack of subtype specification, and need for pathologist review, indicating inadequate presentation of clinical data.

OpenEval R13 evaluates C101-C106 on in vivo experiments and therapeutic implications. Peer R8 evaluates C99-C106. OpenEval finds strong evidence for T-cell-dependent mechanisms but notes therapeutic claims are speculative. Peer reviewers provide strong criticism: no difference in tumor growth (Figure 6E), misleading IHC lacking quantification and pathologist review, need to validate regulatory axis in MFC cells used for experiments. Major disagreement on data quality and interpretation.

Both evaluate summary conclusions C107, C111-C112 on the overall pathway and therapeutic implications. OpenEval finds mechanistic pathway well-established but therapeutic implications speculative. Peer reviewers conclude central claims are not supported due to marginal effects, lack of direct SE causality proof, incomplete data, and observation that ZFP36L1 is not a key PD-L1 stimulant compared to IFNγ. Editor notes this is one of many pathways and data are incomplete. Fundamental disagreement on whether totality of evidence supports conclusions.

OpenEval evaluates background claims C8-C13 on super enhancers, finding them appropriately supported by literature. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background claims.
